claims.quote: Total expenses were $300.7K for June, up 35% over May.
claims.why: All accounts went from $222,208.54 to $300,728.12: +$78,519.58, +35.3%. No cause is stated.

claims.quote: Food purchases rose $18K, reflecting the produce price increases we flagged last quarter.
claims.why: Food purchases went from $33,527.60 to $51,068.40: +$17,540.80, so the amount is right. Produce did not move: Valley Fresh Produce went from $9,731.13 to $9,578.34 (-$152.79). The increase is the new summer meals kits from Sunrise Meal Kits ($17,400, 99%).

claims.quote: Grants to partner agencies rose $48K with the Q4 disbursement to our six partner pantries.
claims.why: Partner agency grants went from $0.00 to $48,000.00: six 'Grant - Q4 FY26 distribution support' payments of $8,000. The vendors are the pantries' own names.

claims.quote: Program salaries were up about 13% on seasonal summer meals staff.
claims.why: Program salaries went from $77,571.35 to $87,281.40: +$9,710.05, +12.5%. The 6/30 'summer meals seasonal (8)' payroll is $9,800, 101% of the change.

claims.quote: Fleet costs rose about $5.5K, nearly all of it the reefer repair on Truck 3.
claims.why: Fleet & fuel went from $3,764.82 to $9,352.88: +$5,588.06. The reefer compressor repair on Truck 3 ($5,600) is 100% of it.

claims.quote: Special events were down $26.6K with the gala behind us in May; the $4.2K Fireside balance that came in this month is the gala's final bill.
claims.why: Special events went from $30,750.00 to $4,200.00: -$26,550.00. May held the Harvest Table gala (venue $14,000, catering deposit $12,300, AV $3,800, auction fee $650); June has only the caterer's final balance ($4,200). The gala's transactions net to -$26,550, 100%. The second figure ($4.2K) is a fact about one invoice, not a variance.

claims.quote: Printing and postage rose $3.2K on the gala invitations.
claims.why: Printing & postage went from $3,500.00 to $6,700.00: +$3,200.00, so the amount is right. The gala invitations and their postage ($2,900 + $600) were in May, the prior period. June's increase is the spring appeal mailing ($4,700 print + $2,000 postage).

claims.quote: Professional fees were up $18K, the year-end accrual for the FY26 audit.
claims.why: Professional fees went from $2,500.00 to $20,500.00: +$18,000.00, exactly the 'Accrue FY26 audit - est. per engagement letter' entry.

claims.quote: Warehouse occupancy fell $2.2K on the landlord's CAM reconciliation credit.
claims.why: Warehouse occupancy went from $10,750.00 to $8,550.00: -$2,200.00, exactly the 'CAM reconciliation 2025 - credit'.

claims.quote: Technology rose $4.4K for the new donor CRM.
claims.why: Technology went from $1,670.00 to $6,020.00: +$4,350.00, so the amount is right. The GiveTrack CRM invoice ($4,400) was credited in full nine days later (grant applied): net $0. The increase is six refurbished laptops ($4,350).

non_claims.quote: We distributed 1.9 million pounds of food in FY26, a record, and the board approved the FY27 budget of $4.1M on June 24.
non_claims.why: Pounds distributed and the budget are not ledger movements.
